This difference is reflected in the smaller decline in transaction mail received compared to transaction mail sent.
In 2015, households in the under 45 age group received an average of about 117 pieces of transactions mail and sent about 22.

Correspondence.text: Households headed by someone under 45 years old received and sent an average of 72 pieces of correspondence mail in 2025, while households headed by someone aged 65 or older received and sent an average of 130 pieces, nearly twice as many .
This effect is presented in Table E.3 , which shows trends in correspondence mail received and sent by age of the householder.
There is not much difference between homeowners and renters for correspondence mail sent, with both groups sending an average of just over 20 pieces in 2025.

Transactions bills payments.text: In 2015, households in the under 45 age group received an average of about 117 pieces of transactions mail and sent about 22.

More evidence of how technological developments are affecting the mail is found in Table E.4 , which shows that household bill payments and household bills and statements received have shifted from the mail to electronic alternatives.
The 65 and over age group saw declines during this period of 35% for transactions received and 61% for transactions sent.

Advertising marketing.text: Focusing on the past ten years, per -household volumes of correspondence mail declined 31%, transaction mail declined 51%, advertising mail declined 40%, and periodicals mail declined 45% .

In addition, the social and economic disruptions caused by the Covid -19 pandemic negatively impacted many mail categories, most substantially advertising mail.

Periodicals.text: Periodicals account for a very small portion of total household mail, about 3%, with many magazines and newspapers transitioning to online formats.

Table E.6 shows that in 2025, households received an average of 22 periodicals, of which 13 were magazines, with newspapers being the second largest periodical category at about 6 pieces per household per year.
Focusing on the past ten years, per -household volumes of correspondence mail declined 31%, transaction mail declined 51%, advertising mail declined 40%, and periodicals mail declined 45% .

Packages.text: Households living in large Metropolitan Statistical Areas (MSAs) received 2% fewer packages in 2025 than in 2015, staying relatively flat, while households living in other MSAs received 68% more packages.
These percentage changes pale in comparison to the 154% increase in the per-household packages received by households living outside of MSAs.

Homeownership.text: The second survey is a mail diary in which households report the volumes and types of mail they received and sent during a given week.
This effect is presented in Table E.3 , which shows trends in correspondence mail received and sent by age of the householder.

The main objectives of the survey are to: • Measure the types and volumes of mail sent and received by U.S. households, • Track trends in mail usage over time, and • Compare mail usage across household demographic characteristics.

Most of this  decline is due to the ongoing shift of mail to various electronic alternatives available online and through  other technologies. In addition, the social and economic disruptions caused by the Covid -19 pandemic  negatively impacted many mail categories, most substantially advertising mail.
